quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A properly-fitted motorcycle allows the rider to:

options.text: Touch the ground with their feet while seated.
Have a seat even with the rider's waist.
Have a seat 10 inches above the rider's waist.
Have a seat 10 inches below the rider's waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Touch the ground with their feet while seated.
questions.explanation: Your feet should touch the ground when you sit on your motorcycle. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests while riding.

questions.question: Before riding, check all of the following except:

options.text: The condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire pressure, tire tread, and the condition of your tire sidewalls and tread surface.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, you should:

options.text: Hold the handgrips loosely to allow for movement.
Hold the handgrips firmly to maintain control.
Use lots of throttle to get over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet so it does not cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly to maintain control.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly when riding over rough surfaces. This keeps you in control of your motorcycle.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance:

options.text: When it is colder than usual.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.explanation: A two-second following distance is normally enough. When roads are wet or icy, increase your following distance because it takes longer to stop.

questions.question: How many drinks can affect a rider's ability to ride?
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride. Never ride a motorcycle after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: To help drivers merge from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Move to the next lane if possible.
Not worry about it since they are merging.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the next lane if possible.
questions.explanation: Drivers may not see your motorcycle when merging. Give them space to merge safely by moving to a different lane if you can.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors while riding?

options.text: More often than you look ahead

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to stay aware of traffic behind you.

questions.question: When a rider's left arm is extended straight out to the left, it means the rider:
questions.explanation: A left arm extended straight out to the left is a hand signal meaning the rider plans to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: The front brake is:

options.text: Only to be used if the rear brake fails.

questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used properly. It provides most of your motorcycle's stopping power—at least three-fourths of the total.

questions.question: Which should you not do to stay safe when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight when possible.

questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed, use your high beam headlight when not near other vehicles, and increase your following distance. Watch vehicles ahead—their lights help show the road and bumps ahead.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more time to stop. Also increase it in heavy traffic or when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: How can you prevent other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve from side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage car drivers from trying to share it with you.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, which is NOT important?
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT standards, fits snugly, and has no cracks or damage. How the helmet looks is not important for safety.

questions.question: When securing a load on your motorcycle, place it:

options.text: On only one side of the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and balanced on both sides. Placing them high or on a sissy bar raises your motorcycle's center of gravity and makes it harder to balance.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.

questions.explanation: A face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for either.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering. They tell you about dangers or road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what formation keeps riders close while staying safe?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps the group together while giving each rider safe space. Use single-file when turning or on curves. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding; it will stop on its own.
Slowly close the throttle to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly close the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when wobbling. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slowly close the throttle to slow down, lean forward and down, and pull off the road. Then find out what caused the wobble.

questions.question: Which sign shape is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular and white with black lettering. These signs tell you the rules you must follow on the road.

questions.question: As a beginning rider, what following distance should you keep?

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.
Do not worry about following distance.
Always ride on the left side so the driver can see you.

questions.explanation: Beginning riders should keep at least four seconds of distance behind other vehicles. Increase this distance when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do to adjust for the extra weight?

options.text: Keep a shorter distance behind other vehicles.
Brake later than you normally would.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. This means your bike will take longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. Ride slower, start braking earlier, leave more space between you and other vehicles, and look for larger gaps when crossing or merging into traffic.

questions.question: After you mount your motorcycle, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check that the mirrors are clean.
Check that the clutch works smoothly.

questions.explanation: Before riding, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes all work properly. Clean and adjust the mirrors. Make sure the fuel supply valve is OPEN, not closed.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's total stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What does eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It does not mean the driver will give you the right of way.
The driver will definitely give you the right of way.
It may make the driver angry.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean the driver will give you the right of way.
questions.explanation: Do not trust eye contact as proof that a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still do not see them.

questions.question: What can cause the front wheel and handlebars to wobble or shake?

options.text: Tire pressure that is not correct.
Brakes that are not working properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tire pressure that is not correct.
questions.explanation: Most wobbles are caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.
